identity.title: Scaling Collapse Reveals Universal Dynamics in Compute-Optimally Trained Neural Networks

problem.claim: Understand neural network training dynamics at scale.

gap.claim: Complex interactions among architectures, optimizers, and data make predictive theory challenging.

contributions.claim: Shows that compute-optimally trained models exhibit precise collective regularities, including universal loss-curve collapse under end-of-training normalization.
Identifies “supercollapse,” a tighter collapse with learning-rate decay that appears across schedules, datasets, and architectures, including next-token-prediction transformers.
Connects collapse to power-law neural scaling laws and analyzes an SGD-noise model intended to capture schedule-induced curve deformation and variance suppression.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors name the exceptionally tight normalized loss-curve collapse enabled by learning-rate decay “supercollapse.”

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that loss curves across model sizes collapse onto one universal curve after compute and loss are normalized to unity at training end.
The authors report that, with learning-rate decay, normalized-curve discrepancies fall below individual models’ seed-level noise floor, and observe this across schedules, datasets, and architectures.
The authors report that collapse breaks down under suboptimal hyperparameter scaling, suggesting it can indicate proper scaling.

narrative_sequence.summary: Frames large-scale training dynamics as an open problem complicated by interacting design choices.
Reports universal loss-curve collapse after normalizing compute and loss at training end.
Introduces supercollapse under learning-rate decay and reports it across schedules, datasets, and architectures.
Reports breakdown under suboptimal hyperparameter scaling, making collapse a proposed practical scaling indicator.
Links the phenomena to scaling-law power laws and an SGD-noise dynamics model, including the proposed role of learning-rate decay.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs a normalized cross-model regularity with a failure mode under suboptimal scaling and then offers a mechanistic account involving SGD noise and learning-rate schedules.

lessons.interpretation: A compact paper narrative can align an observable diagnostic, its boundary condition, and an explanatory model.
lessons.application: When presenting a scaling phenomenon, define the normalization, show where the pattern breaks, and connect both the pattern and failure mode to a proposed mechanism.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the study has no explicit diagnostic boundary condition or mechanistic analysis.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact compute and loss normalization procedure beyond end-of-training unity, or quantify model sizes and collapse errors.
The criteria for compute-optimal versus suboptimal hyperparameter scaling are not given.
The abstract does not provide experimental counts, datasets, architectures, schedules, or details sufficient to assess the SGD-noise model quantitatively.
